# OMEM

> The open-source (MIT) system of record for what an AI agent believed and did. OMEM keeps
> both sides of a contradiction, tracks what an agent believed and when, answers
> "why" with a provenance chain, and puts a human approval step before a risky
> action runs. Self-hosted, one `pip install omem-infrastructure`, no
> dependencies, dashboard included. It phones home to nobody (CI-asserted).

OMEM is for two audiences: builders who want agent memory that never silently
overwrites a contradiction, and teams shipping agents to clients who must answer
"why did the agent do that" with an audit trail and gate risky actions behind a
named human approver. The engine is frozen and replays byte-identically, so an
upgrade can never rewrite recorded history. Its wider objective: teach AI what
people are like while holding a fact about no one, via anonymous behavioural
priors (counts, never people) that consenting installs pool into a training
corpus.

## Docs

- [Quickstart](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/docs/quickstart/): install and first belief in about a minute
- [Documentation](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/docs/): the memory model, verbs, and concepts
- [SDK reference](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/docs/sdk/): the nine verbs of the Python SDK

## Product

- [Accountability](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/accountability/): prove why the agent acted, approve before it does
- [Objective](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/objectives/): teach AI what people are like, holding a fact about no one
- [The commons](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/commons/): the shared bank itself, live figures included; what a line contains, what contributing does and does not buy a contributor, and the measured conditions under which it stops paying
- [The claims ledger](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/claims/): every load-bearing sentence next to the executable statement that would go red if it stopped being true, generated from CLAIMS.md so the page cannot drift from the file CI checks
- [Security](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/security/): what is implemented today and what is not built yet
- [Pricing](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/pricing/): free and MIT while in beta

## Specification

- [The Testimony Record Specification v0.1](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/spec/testimony-record/): the open format for what an AI agent believed, what it was allowed to do, and who allowed it; four conformance levels, free to implement
- [Read a Testimony Record](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/spec/testimony-record/view): drop a record in and read what the agent believed, where each belief came from, where it disagreed with itself, and what it was allowed to do. Beliefs resolve to the evidence under them; a belief supported by nothing says so rather than being dropped; contradictions are drawn as pairs because two rows that disagree look like two rows unless something says they are about the same claim. The conformance level is computed as the file loads and every level is reported separately, so a level that is satisfied but gated behind an unmet one below stays visible. Runs a TypeScript port of the reference validator, held to agreement with it by a test over valid and invalid records. Everything happens in the browser: the file is read, checked and drawn in the tab and there is no endpoint to send it to.
- [Emitting a Testimony Record](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/spec/testimony-record/emitting): how to emit a conforming record from a system you already have. The record is a translation of facts most memory systems already store rather than a change to how anything works, and for a system that only records it is an afternoon. Worked example against an ordinary two-table store of sources and facts, with the mapping from what you keep to the six entry types, and the two mistakes a first record usually makes: passing your own vocabulary through where the evidence kinds are a closed list, and emitting entries out of time order. Declaring that your system does not act satisfies the gate requirements by having nothing to gate, so a record-only system can still reach TR-4. No dependency on any particular software; the validator is one standard-library file you can copy.
- [Testimony Record implementations](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/spec/testimony-record/implementations): which systems emit conforming records, the level each reaches, and how to get listed; listings follow a record that passed the validator, never self-report
- [Agent audit-readiness check](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/agent-audit-check): eleven questions about what an AI agent actually records, scored in the browser against the four Testimony Record levels; no upload, no signup, returns the level reached and the specific gaps
- [Installing a licence](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/docs/licence): how an OMEM enterprise licence is installed and verified; verification is offline with no callback and no telemetry, and an expired licence stops unlocking paid components without stopping the server
- [For your vendor security review](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/vendor-review): supplier answers for procurement, not just software controls; no data leaves your infrastructure, no subprocessors, no telemetry, MIT core you keep permanently if the supplier stops existing, and a plain list of where the review will fail
- [JSON Schema](https://infrastructure.omem-cloud.com/testimony-record-v0.1.schema.json)
